utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Good morning, Mr. Djukic. Mr. Djukic, I would like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you have given yesterday; that is, that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: There is a problem in the booths, a technical problem in the booths. No power or something. We've called the technicians in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that results in the witness not receiving translation. Is that -- apparently, looking at your face ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic, you hear me in English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nein.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we'll -- do you receive any interpretation. Then we'll have to wait.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We have temporarily resolved the problem. Pending a technician's arrival, we can probably start.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The interpreter has just said something, Your Honour. Interpreter has just said that we can -- they have temporarily resolved the problem [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand that the problem has been temporarily resolved?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, from the B/C/S booth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately not for us. We are not receiving interpretation B/C/S -- no, now we can hear interpretation in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will do the final check. Mr. Djukic, can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we can continue. I then repeat what I said earlier, is that I would like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given yesterday that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Petrovic will now resume. Mr. Petrovic, you announced yesterday that you would need -- was it 20 minutes or half an hour?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I asked for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have half an hour. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Djukic.

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I would like to remind you again at the start, the problem -- of the problem that we had yesterday, the speed of speech and overlapping, so please try to remember to pause and to speak more slowly.

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I believe that I've already adjusted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djukic, we whether briefly now go back to the Ilok events. You spoke about them yesterday extensively. And in that context, let me ask you do you know who Colonel Dusan Grahovac is?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He is the chief of the security organ of the Slavonia Baranja Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we take a look at document 2D168. This is a report compiled by Colonel Dusan Grahovac, the security and intelligence organ of the Slavonia Baranja Command -- Corps Command. If we could look at -- we have the first page before us, but could we see page 2, please, in both versions, both in B/C/S and in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness I will read out a portion of this document and ask you whether you know anything about this incident. "On the 27th of February, 1993, at 1500 hours, the Catholic church in Ilok was blocked by the Red Berets in the presence of Vojin Susa, minister of justice in the RSK. And this was done after information leaked that the Catholic priest Fra Marko Malovic, on the premises of the church received certain persons. The church was searched and no one was found." Mr. Djukic, this event as described here occurred a few days before your arrival in the area. Could you please tell us, once you arrived that area, did you hear anything about the events mentioned by Grahovac here?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear anything about it. Later on, I had occasion -- I had occasion to communicate with Fra Marko, and the -- the priest there, and we had very good relations, but I didn't know anything about this event.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, do you know anything about the second part of this report. I'd like to ask you about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that's under 3 in the middle of that paragraph where it reads: "The Red Berets from Ilok were reformed and now they were group AA and placed under the command on the 45th Brigade. And they operate as an IDG. So far, they have done all the training in shooting, with side-arms, and they are also being trained as part of the 453rd Mechanised Brigade from Sremska Mitrovica." Witness, sir, could you help us? Do you know which 4 -- 45th [as interpreted] brigade is referred to here?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is the brigade that I mentioned yesterday, and I believe it -- this relates to the same unit that was mentioned yesterday as having been formed by President Hadzic, at the head of which was Susan [phoen]. The only thing I don't know is what Sremska Mitrovica has to do with it. That part of know nothing about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We do not have the screens on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honour, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The interpreters inform us that they do not have their screen on. Is there a way to resolve that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We can work without the screens but we just wanted to make you aware of the issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I'd like to urge our technicians to resolve that problem as well. Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, unless I'm mistaken, this document wasn't noticed to us in advance, so I'd like some time to look into it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, is that the case?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that we noticed all the documents. We notified the Prosecution, and if we made an omission, my apologies. And, of course, although this is a document on our 65 ter list and had obviously been received by the Prosecution, we don't mind if we have a moment for the Prosecutor to get acquainted with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Perhaps it could be MFI'd so I could like into it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Registrar, the number assigned to this document would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D763. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D763 is marked for identification. If possible, could we hear later today from you, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, we will now go back to where we left off yesterday; namely, the Skorpions and your activity in that respect. Mr. Djukic, at one point, were you assigned to inspect the operations of the oil industry in Krajina?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was in charge of operations because I am familiar with police work and crime investigations. Now, in this particular case, two inspectors arriving from Knin. They were economists, and they were able to inspect the financial dealings of the company; whereas, I was only there in order to assist them in drafting a report and possibly a criminal complaint, if that was required.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic, were there any reasons to expect that there would be some sort of clash with the security of the oil industry in Dzeletovci?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Slobodan Medic, also known as Boca, informed the duty officer at the Secretariat of The interior in Vukovar, which was the organ that had jurisdiction in that area, as well as subject matter jurisdiction. He said that he would not allow the inspectors to enter the premises of the NIT.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I -- again, I have an issue about notice. There was absolutely no notice about this report, about this investigation the witness undertook. The only thing that's mentioned about the Skorpions is that the witness, having been chief police inspector, knows that the Skorpions were a military formation and will confirm that the Skorpions and Arkan's unit were not units of the RS DB -- of Republic of Serbia DB. That was all that was noticed about the Skorpions. Now, the witness's involvement in this kind of investigation is something that we certainly could have investigated had we known that this was going to be part of his evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness is here to explain how and why they were not within the remit of the accused. And these are the facts that point to that effect. I did not expect my -- I don't think my colleague expected that they would come and -- that a witness would come and say, no, they didn't do this, or they did that. I -- the witness can only present the facts as he sees them, on the basis of which the Trial Chamber can then draw relevant conclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. I have to say, generally speaking -- with the 65 ters of the Simatovic Defence, generally speaking we do have quite a bit of detail. I have to say that. I think this particular 65 ter summary was very lacking in detail. It -- the time-periods are unclear, the -- what the witness will actually say is very unclear, and these are very generalised topics. In this particular instance, Your Honours, this is -- this is quite a -- a very direct example. I didn't stand up again yesterday; although, a lot of the evidence, I would say, was basically a surprise to use because we didn't know it from the summary. We are hesitant to make this kind of submission so are -- we understand that a lot of the information comes in the summaries. In this instance, Your Honour, really we had no notice of this particular aspect which I find quite a critical aspect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, there seems to be some merit in the observations made by Ms. Marcus. Now, I suggest that we continue for the time being, and that Ms. Marcus will consider whether or not she needs more time to prepare for cross-examination; or, for a re-call of the witness at a later stage. We'll consider that once we've heard the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you may proceed, Mr. Petrovic. But what was just read to us as what the witness could tell us certainly does not -- is not -- his operational activities, his investigations, but rather general statements. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, the last thing you said to us was that Medic said that he would not allow inspectors to enter the premises of the NIK, the oil industry of Krajina. Can you now tell us, please, did you know -- or did you inform the military authorities about the activities that you intended to undertake at the NIK?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may just clarify something. Even had the Defence asked me --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I have to interfere. Could you please just answer my question.

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, then, I will clarify there was no reason for me to inform the military authorities that I was about to conduct an investigation of some economic issues in an economic company.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic, at some point in time, did you go to Dzeletovci for some talks?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Zarkovic suggested that we go there. And to finally resolve this issue with Boca, I do have to go back, I think -- if you understood correctly what I said, that there were two teams -- or, rather, two ways in which the Skorpions acted. One of them was a military arm and the other one was classic security, which is part of the interior, Ministry of Interior. I wanted to avoid a conflict - although we had an elite unit; Bosko Drazic, who was a specialist, was at the head of it - and I proposed that Zarkovic and I go to Dzeletovci unarmed, just the two of us. We arrived there, and we found these people very rough -- their feathers were very ruffled. They were fully armed. They were upset about our being there, why were we sending people, what did we want, they were working for the state and so on. I presented all the facts to them. I said that this had nothing to do with him. And I don't want to go over the entire conversation then, but I had three meetings with him. I resolved all three of them without the use of force, and I have to stress that my strong side is that I was able to resolve matters by just talking to people where others would have to use force.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we get a time-period that this refers to? At least a year, perhaps a month.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic, when was this control ordered by the Knin leadership and when did you had this first conversation with Medic about an inspection of the business practices of NIK?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that yesterday that the action was planned and initiated on the 15th of January, 1994, and lasted until the 5th of February of the same year.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And after you talked with Medic, was it possible to inspect the NIK company and what were the results of the inspection and what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The government of the Krajina simply established by the income to the budget that the funds were not coming in at the previous pace. The inspectors determined that there were fictional payments to a construction firm from Ruma. It was a large amount of money. I don't remember exactly what it was, and that the Skorpions and other workers who were -- worked on physical and technical security besides salaries, which were routed through the SDK, the public accounting service, they were also paid significant amounts in cash personally. Then we found out receipts from which we saw that Slobodan Medic and his team received a certain quantity of fuel for their vehicles and sometimes also for their friends. Criminal charges were submitted against Dusan who is from Ruma and also Vukasin Egic, the contractor from Ruma. Already he was quite well off at that time in Novi Sad, who had built for his needs and for his business a large number of real estate. The charges were submitted to the district public prosecutor office, Egic resorted to his immunity because he was a deputy of the assembly of the -- assembly of the Serbian Krajina. It was suggested that the assembly at the first session revokes this immunity with the remark that this was a subject which was liable for prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes. At page 10, lines 18 and 19, the witness mentioned some dates which were not recorded in the transcript. Could that please be repeated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat. You said, "I said that the," and then a part is missing, "and lasted until the 5th of February of the same year." Could you repeat what you said at the beginning of that answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 15th of January we finished in Ilok and we moved to Dzeletovci.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you just please tell us the year?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And -- thank you. And can you tell us for the transcript so that it's all clear who Egic is, what was his post?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vukasin Egic is the previous director of the oil industry. He went to Novi Sad with his family, but he continued with the new director to get involved in dealings to appropriate funds. The problem was in the fact that we extracted raw oil and gave it to Pancevo, and then you could never control how much oil was extracted and how many additives were received.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. You mentioned something about financing of the Skorpions unit. I would like to ask you, if you know, who the Skorpions received their salaries from?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They received a very modest salary from the Army of the Republic of the Krajina, and they also received cash without any record being made of it from NIK. They would receive that at their cashier's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Do you know if any of the high-ranking officials of the Serbian MUP visited Medic while you were in that area?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Medic's house was in Sremski Banovci. It's a short distance away from Dzeletovci. It's a prominent respectable family. His father was the king of cattle, and many officials from Sid and Mitrovica would stop by to visit him and those from the public security service. A frequent guest of his was Radovan Stojicic, Badza, with the mediation of a certain Milovan Terzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic, do you know if any point the Skorpions were sent to the Kordun front?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know they were sent to the Kordun front.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how this came about? How did it come about that they left for the Kordun front?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a decision by the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska in Knin, in Krajina, and it was justified by the fact that western Bosnia and Fikret Abdic needed to be reinforced because if our position -- so that our position in Kordun could be strengthened.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic, what was the rank that Medic held, if he had any rank, when you met him first; and did he, at any point receive a promotion?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time I saw Medic in uniform was in the rank of major. The next time he was lieutenant-colonel. I don't know what his previous advancement in the army was like.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And do you know if there were any reactions to the promotion of Medic to the rank of lieutenant-colonel?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were reactions. The association of military war veterans of Srem sent a letter to a number of an addresses, including that of General Momcilo Perisic. He was, at the time, the chief of the armed forces. I think it was still Yugoslavia at that time. Actually, no, I know that it was for a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us what the letter said; if you know?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. That -- it said that he had been given the rank of Vojvoda, Stanko, that Miroljub Vujovic was given a rank, this Medic was given a rank, and I can also mention that all three of them were tried for war crimes and sentenced to long prison sentences. The surname of Stanko was Vujanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you please tell us in a few sentences only how long the Skorpions stayed in the Srem Baranja area and when and under which conditions did they leave?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Skorpions left in September 1996 at the insistence of the transitional administer, Mr. Klein, who wanted to expel them from the area because the population there objected to their behaviour. Their arrogant behaviour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us how they left?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I went with a couple of associates and I told them that the oil wells were closed, that they had nothing more to do there, that they were not needed. On the 15th of June we were completely disarmed pursuant to the resolution, and no army other than police forces and the military component of the UNTAES was permitted to stay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic, you said that the wells were closed. Do you know upon whose instructions they were shut down?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were shut down by Milanovic, Milan Milanovic, aka Mrgud. Vojislav Stanimirovic, the president of the district council, and President Goran Hadzic went to Mrgud, and together they asked to be received by President Slobodan Milosevic. And they told him, Mr. President, how are we going to live? What are we going to live on? We don't have any more oil. And the president asked them -- he asked Mrgud, Mrgud what is that? And he said ironically, The president, just that little one. And that's how we were left without income. It's true that Mr. Klein insisted on that, too, and he sent information to Franjo Tudjman that he was giving him the oil fields or the wells as a present for his birthday.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you know if any unit by Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, if any of his units were there in that area when you came to Srem and Slavonia and Baranja?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In April, only a month after I had arrived, the minister, Milan Martic, convened the political action board - all the more responsible people from the Dalj municipality. And he said, As of today, the entry is banned to the region of Republika Srpska as a whole to Mr. Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, and three other active inspectors of the Ministry of Interior of the state of Serbia. I note it was public security, and the inspectors were from Zagreb, which means that they were under my control before, under my command.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And after this decision by Minister Martic, did any people -- any Arkan's people remain in the area? Did he continue to develop his jobs there in the area?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. For the purposes of the operation of his company, which was properly registered, he planted some watermelon fields which was controlled by Milanovic. There were people of his there who were maintaining his personal buildings in Erdut, but it was a small number of them. They were not in uniform and did not cause any problems, other than some red caps that they were wearing, which were turned back to front.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic at any point in time during that year, was there a reconciliation between Arkan and Minister Martic?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. With the mediation of Milanovic they met in Belgrade. They exchanged kisses. And Minister Martic allowed him to return but not to Erdut but to a holiday resort of the Osijek Elektroslavonija, which is right near the bridge when you cross over from Vojvodina to the Srem Baranja area. This was also a very nice facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us exactly where Arkan was allowed to go back again with his men? Just that location.

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's Erdut. But not where he was earlier in the centre for the TO centre. This is where our units were located now and where we were having our seminars, but he was near the bridge close to the Danube river, close to the holiday resort of the electric utility company.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When you returned to the area, who was commanding Arkan's unit; do you know?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Loncar. Although he was always closer to Milanovic. They didn't have any particular disagreements, Milanovic and Loncar, although Loncar was a little bit uncomfortable because he had to be subordinated to practically a civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic, do you know if any part of the Serbian Volunteer Guards of Arkan's were sent to the Kordun front?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were sent there together. As I explained already, a part of the regular police force were sent, eight of whom were killed, and that minister -- deputy minister, Rade Kostic, too. On the 11th November, the policemen were there -- were killed. And on the 12th of November, Rade Kostic was, and the circumstances of that were never explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, when you say there were sent together, who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mean Medic. I mentioned him before. I meant his unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic, do you know where Pajzos is. Do you know what it is?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a prominent building, a little bit neglected. It was neglected then. But it's been 15 years since then, perhaps it's been fixed up.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And do you know what happened at Pajzos? What was there when you came to that area?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Electronic equipment. It was a listening centre, and I was not responsible for that centre nor was I well versed in what was going on there. I did not have access to it. I as the chief inspector of the Croatian police could not enter this cryptographic centre because you needed a special permit and signature in order to go in.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm looking at the clock. And this is why perhaps why I'm rushing a little bit. Mr. Djukic, are you able to tell us, do you know who this wire-tapping centre belonged to; if you know?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. To the Army of the Republic of the Serbian Krajina and partly to the state security of our republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And do you know who provided the security for Pajzos when you were in the area?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Soldiers in camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Just two more questions, Witness. In 1995, some police units from the Republic of Serbia came to the area.

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know about that. The police brigade in Erdut had -- half of their active police component had to be separated off because we were expecting a military action from Croatia and two people --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- agreed with the chief of the public security service, Vlastimir Djordjevic. They made an agreement with him. And General Obrad Stevanovic was sent with about a thousand policemen. These were employees who were working on regular duties but were put together in special police units, and these units are formed according to the rota principle; a secretariat would provide ten, another secretariat would provide 20 men, and then in this way you would form a company and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, I would just like to ask you for the transcript to repeat who agreed with whom about this and who was sent. This is not clear from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The agreement was made between the deputy minister at the proposal of the commander of our police brigade for special tasks and Milan Milanovic with Vlastimir Djordjevic, the chief or assistant chief of the MUP of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You said that a unit was sent from Serbia. Under whose command was this police unit from Serbia that came to the area?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was under the command of General Obrad Stevanovic who was in charge of special units within the Serbian MUP, and for a long time -- over a long period of time I carried out assignments, including in Kosovo, together with him, and we had a very good relationship. I knew him very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic, which department did those policemen who had come from Serbia belong to?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, those police officers were from the public security department. That's a generally known fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us if you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I regret that all this information that we are having now is also nowhere in the 65 ter summary. I just had to notice that. This is also another entire aspect: Obrad Stevanovic is not mentioned, the witness's involvement in Kosovo is not mentioned, deployment of a group of police officials from Serb is not mentioned. In fact, 1995 is not mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you allow me, in our original 65 ter summary, we do not mention this. However, the summary that we forwarded a day before yesterday it was mentioned, and it arose from the proofing of this witness; Obrad Stevanovic, the year 1995. Kosovo, that's true, was not mentioned, but that's something that the witness said right now answering spontaneously my questions and is probably not relevant to this case in any case, and it relates to the 1980s of the previous century.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, 1981.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it's true. In the e-mail it says: "The witness will testify in deployment of PJP units from Serbia. In the second part of 1995, PJP units were under the command of Obrad Stevanovic." The detail was not in there but that was the information that we did receive, so the fact that the name "Stevanovic" was not in the 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are now on the list of those who has to slow down on the speed of speech.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. Yes, so we did receive the name "Stevanovic." We didn't know the details at all, but that was noticed to us in an e-mail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You say there was some notice although at a very late stage. Yes. I keep all your observations in the back of the Chamber's mind, and we'll see what consequences, if any, have to be drawn from them. Mr. Petrovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, do you know who financed the sending and stay of these police officers from Serbia in Srem and Baranja in 1995?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. I had nothing to do with finances within the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. Mr. Jordash, could you give us an estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Up to two hours, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'd like to urge the parties that we see that we conclude the testimony of this witness this week. Please proceed. Mr. Djukic, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Jordash. Mr. Jordash is counsel for Mr. Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me first ask you about your time as the chief inspector of the police of the RSK beginning in March of 1993. I want to try to understand the structure of the police or the Ministry of Interior of the RSK at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have on the screen, please, 1D05458.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It's a map. And I'm hoping that this helps you to explain a little more about the principle figures and the structure of the MUP at that point. Now, does this map show many of the principal locations where significant structures of the RSK MUP were based in 1993, when you came to take your post?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you are missing western Dalmatia. You only have up to Vojnic. You're showing the area up to Vojnic. But perhaps can you move the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You're saying that there were significant locations to the west of Vojnic. Is that -- do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I will start by what I see here. Let's move on from --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the bottom left on the map. Knin, the Ministry of the Interior. And -- that's the headquarters of the service, Korenica; Secretariat of the Interior for Lika, Vojnic; Secretariat of the Interior for Kordun, Glina; Secretariat of the Interior for Banja, Okucani; a small organisational unit of the ministry and the Secretariat of the Interior; Beli Manastir, Secretariat of the Interior and the police station in Darda, Vukovar. A police station in Markusica; a police station in Ilok; a police station in Mirkovci; and a police station in Tovarnik; as well as a police department in Vukovar for public security on the Danube river; Borovo Naselje; an outpost or branch unit of the Ministry of the Interior. And it was my headquarters as well as a team of specialists that were under me. You are not showing --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What was the name you just mentioned, Mr. Djukic?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned Benkovac. Kistanje there was a police station. Perhaps you can find it you on the map here, let me just take a look. Well, it's a small town so it's possible it's not even on the map itself, but you have to find Benkovac. It should be on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we'll find that later. Now we've got it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is on the map, just west of Knin. Benkovac. And Kistanje is, as far as I understand, somewhere between Knin and Benkovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned secretariats.

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Where did -- what was the significance of the secretariats within the overall structure?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Secretariats were the basic organisational units of the ministry. The service was centralised along vertical lines, and the secretariats were in charge of the basic work; whereas, the ministry acted as an inspection -- it had an inspecting and co-ordinating role of the secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Where did you fit into the system? Who was above you, what was the structure above you, and, briefly, what was the structure below?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my subordinate throughout this time was Mr. Ilija Kojic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: My superior was Nikola Kojic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But it would take a long time for me to mention all the subordinates. There was only --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the name of the subordinate.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Who was the subordinate you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milan Corak. He was an analyst and he prepared a newspaper, professional newspaper, the 2nd of May 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Let's forget subordinates for now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, can we get clarification of the names that were just mentioned a few lines earlier, earlier on page 23, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think we only had one name mentioned, Milan Corak, unless I missed something.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: There were two different first names.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, what -- I'm not following my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see Ilija Kojic and Nikola Kojic on -- but that's a --

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: This -- there were several questions put at page 23, line 2. I'm not sure which one the witness was answering about the superior, the subordinate, et cetera. I think it's -- it's quite unclear, the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me clarify. I think that it's relatively clear, but I can make sure it's absolutely clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Kojic was your superior. Is that what you just testified to? Ilija Kojic.

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kojic was the assistant minister and he was appointed to that post by the Government of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. In other words, he was an official. I was an operative of the service and the chief inspector not only in this area but for the entire territory of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, and there were a number of inspectors who were my employees but people came and went. It would take too long for me to mention all of their names. For instance, the person who stayed longer was Mile Pavkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what was Kostic to you, Radovan Kostic? Did he have a relation to you?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rade Kostic was appointed assistant minister by the Government of the Republic of Serbian Krajina after my time, and Mr. Martic sent a telegram - addressing it to me - asking that I promote this appointment of Kostic's, that we should inform the public on who it was that we were appointing in the service, that we should try and be open and transparent in our work.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Was Kojic in real terms your supervisor, or were you left to get on with the job? What was the situation?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That -- his role was totally clear. Kojic was an official, a public official. He was a representative of the ministry before other competent organs. He would approve all our contacts with the public media. He was in charge of material and logistical security of the service -- or, rather, provisions of the service, and in charge of other duties such as contacts with various assemblies, with the command, and similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Was his role at that point in time - and I'm talking about March of 1993 and thereabouts - anything to do with being a police officer, commanding police officers on the ground, or much more?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you finish your question --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you finish your question and then we'll hear from Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]... or much more in the role as you've just described which appears to be kind of quasi-political?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Before you answer the question, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that the year did not make it into the transcript. My colleague mentioned one year, whereas the witness received another year through interpretation, so I think it would be only fair to clarify it for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat what year you mentioned, Mr. Jordash, and explain that to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We're talking about March of 1993 at the time you began in the RSK as secretary -- or as inspector, I beg your pardon, and I'm asking about Kojic's role. Do you follow what I'm asking you?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I understand what you're asking. The organigram and the structure of the Ministry of Interior is very well known to me, and as an assistant minister, he had a role - and it is not a dysfunctional role by any means - he was, for all practical purposes, minister. In the absence of Minister Martic, he would be the one who would employ new officials, who would issue disciplinary measures, who would approve leave, and so on. There's a lot of other -- there's a lot of other work that he would be in charge of, such as personnel and finances and so on. He would -- and we reported to him on all our operations and what goals we had reached. Simply put, he was -- he had a political role. He was the politician within the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Kostic. Was -- what his actual role at the time you -- go ahead.

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was also assistant minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And was his job at that time more in the role as quasi-politician or as a police officer?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was nothing quasi in my service, sir. We dealt with serious matters, and Kostic was in charge of the entire territory; whereas, Kojic was only in charge of Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What do you mean Kostic was in charge of the entire territory. Which territory are you including within that?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Republic of Serbian Krajina. We've just looked at the map of its territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What kind of reputation did Kostic have as a police officer?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kostic was one of the best commanders, police station commanders. While I was the chief in Croatia, he was based in Darda. Darda was significant. He could have gone up in the service because there was a very prominent hunting ground in that area which was visited by various government officials and -- and even foreign heads of state and government, so it was important to have a person who was aware of protocol who would know how to deal with these matters; otherwise, he would have been appointed to a higher post. But for us it was more important to have a commander of his calibre there than, for instance, in Virovitica where the chief operative had control of the territory of 130.000 inhabitants. He went through a lot of training. He went to the higher school of --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So you've said two things which I want to ask you about with Kostic. You said on the one hand he was in charge of the entire territory, and other hand he was based in Darda. And you seem to suggest he was the -- a police commander.

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you misunderstood. I said that Rade Kostic in the one-time Republic of Croatia, before Krajina seceded, he was in that post, and he was a high professional. So there was nothing that would be foreign to him in the public security affairs part of the service.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to -- now we've set out some of the background. I want to ask you to comment, if you can, on a number of exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Please, could we have on the screen D398, under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: As you'll see, it's a report from the Federal Secretariat of National Defence to the Ministry of Interior, to Jovica Stanisic, and it's a report containing security-related intelligence, dated the 19th of February, 1993. And if we go to the second page, we will see the date that the report appears to have been written, is the 18th of February, 1993. If you just read the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my apologies for interrupting. But the first page of this document is not actually the Federal Secretariat of National Defence. If we look at the stamp we will see that it's something totally different. In other words, the translation is not correct. If you look at the original, you will see that it does not say Federal Secretariat of National Defence in the heading. So this may confuse the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can see that it is from the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me have a look. What I see in the English at this moment does not correspond with what I see in the B/C/S. Dates are different. Could we first have the ... Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: When I open this in my e-court system, I see a different B/C/S version which has other stamps on it that are not visible in this B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Apparently the English version of what we are looking at does not correspond with the B/C/S. And now I think it seems to be the same, what we have on our screen now. Yes. Now we have two corresponding pages, although there is a ... I think we could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- proceed on this basis. But I'm trying to --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think when we see, Your Honour, the end - and this is something I should have noticed earlier - when we see who it's from, who the author of the document is, we have some idea who is sending the document and --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps I can help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you can, please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you look at the stamp that is in the upper left corner, it reads, from what I can see, the Secretariat of the Internal Affairs, or interior, which was translated as Federal Secretariat of National Defence. As far as I can see, that's the entire problem, mistranslation of that portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, at least we have now on our screens two corresponding pages. Mr. Petrovic draws our attention to a possible mistranslation of the badly legible stamp on the left top corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do note the time. I wonder if the witness might be given this. I'm going to spend quite some time on this document, if I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes -- [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: As I hope the witness will know something about the events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you then provide him with a hard copy so that he can read it during the break. Mr. Djukic, you have some homework to do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, that's the 19th of February. But I only arrived there on the 15th of March, so I wouldn't know anything about this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave it in the hands of Mr. Jordash, whether he wants to verify whether the witness has any knowledge of what is in there before he gives you the task of reading the document, but ... Mr. Jordash, if there would be any question in this moment which might help us out for after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What I want to ask you about -- what I'm interested in, Mr. Witness, are the relations between characters such as Miroljub Vujovic, Ilija Kojic, Arkan, Mrgud, and a dispute between Vukovar MUP and -- and an Arkan-led administration around Erdut. Are these matters which you might be able to help us with?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could help you with that. Because when it was being discussed that I should go to Vukovar, Minister Martic told me that Arkan had burst onto the premises of the Secretariat of the Internal Affairs, and I don't know what the outcome was, whether there were any casualties, whether there were any dead, any wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, may I take it that you still invite the witness to read this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a three-page report. The real content seems to be on pages 2 and 3. Would you be so kind to read this report. A hard copy will be provided to you during the break. We will resume at a quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, if you're ready to proceed, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You read the document; am I correct? And you need to put the headphones on. It's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just -- just remain -- if we need assistance, the usher will help us out.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Are you there and comfortable, Mr. Djukic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The line of sight is obstructed for good reasons.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Djukic, did you read the document, and can I proceed to ask you some questions about it?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Please go ahead. I'll welcome them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's go to page 2 of the document in English and B/C/S. Now, let's go through the document paragraph by paragraph, because the -- what it purports to describe may be quite significant. "On 16th of February this year, there was an attempt at forcibly removing the leadership of the MUP of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, the Vukovar secretariat." Do you know if that's correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that it's correct and it's up to the Chamber to decide whether we would need to discuss about these fights and these crimes in the context of crimes of war. And if that is deemed appropriate, I will continue to discuss that and talk about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's very nice of you to give the authority to the Chamber, whether or not to do this. But if you listen to the questions put to you by Mr. Jordash and answer them, then we'll proceed. And if there's any problem, either the Chamber, or Ms. Marcus, or Mr. Petrovic will intervene. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Is it correct that there was an attempt by - let me say, first of all - Arkan and men around him, to remove the leadership, or part of the leadership, of the RSK MUP?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely correct, true.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Looking at paragraph 2, a description there of the reserve of force of the RSK Army, headed by Miroljub Vujovic, the secretary of the Secretariat of National Defence of Vukovar, taking over the MUP building. Is that correct? Did that happen?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what happened. Miroljub Vujovic in the Ministry of Defence for the town of Vukovar and his superior, as assistant minister, is Milan Milanovic. He has been mentioned 100 times already; aka Mrgud. I could continue without giving trouble to you. I could go through the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Wait for the questions that Mr. Jordash will put to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know if this attempt to remove part of the RSK MUP involved part of the RSK Army in conjunction with men under Arkan?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We all know that. It states that he took 120 or 150 armed members of the reserve forces of the RSK army from the lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic, so you understand what we're doing here, I'm asking you from your personal knowledge whether you can corroborate what's in the document or whether your personal knowledge is different to what's in the document. So -- so when I ask you whether, according to you, from your knowledge, this involved members of the RSK army in conjunction with the -- Arkan, I want you to inform the Court what your knowledge is and whether it's -- corresponds with what's in the document.

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My information fits in completely with that, with the note that I don't know if it was 90 or 120 or 130. In any case, this is something that -- from that -- that turned from a crowd into a mob.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And was Arkan in command of this operation?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Arkan joined later. He was in command -- actually, Miroljub Vujovic was in command of the operation, quote/unquote. He is a serious criminal from Ovcara. From the day before -- you can see in the information it says that at the Ilok border crossing, he crashed through the barrier under influence of alcohol, and he did not want to give his ID to the police so that they could conduct an inquiry and prosecute him and have the damages compensated.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Vujovic is -- you mentioned Ovcara, he is man who has been convicted of war crimes in relation to Ovcara in the Belgrade War Crimes Court; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. He is one of the most serious -- that is one of the most serious crimes in this war, after Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, how was it that Vujovic was able to command part of the RSK Army? What was his command authority in relation to them?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I did answer. Perhaps I wasn't clear. He was the chief of the part of the ministry responsible for the municipality of Vukovar for mobilisation and recruiting tasks, and Milanovic was his superior. And he could have very easily gotten together 100 people. He is a paramilitary member. He is a criminal; sniper, a shooter. And he had his supporters among those who are similar to him, drunks and thugs. He enjoyed their support. I cannot say that he enjoyed their confidence and trust.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can I just have a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Let's keep going through the document and some of these issues we can revisit as appropriate. Who do you know were in the -- was in the building when the RSK army, or part of it, surrounded the building?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a smaller number of employees. It was mostly duty work and preparations. Two policemen were in Ilok at the police station on specified tasks. This was Djukic and Grbic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Who was Vujovic aiming for? Who are his targets? Who did he want to remove?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's evident, Kojic, Djukic and other functionaries, and he did find adequate substitutions for him, or replacements.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We can see there in paragraph 6 of the English --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We need to go to page 2, I think, of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Where it says, "After a five-hour discussion..." Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him. Actually, I -- I studied it. I -- I reviewed it, and I noted what I needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go through this as the paragraphs appear so we don't get confused. Do you know, looking at the paragraph which begins: "The commander of the Slavonia Corps of the RSK Army was also informed of this incident and stated that he was not aware of the situation and that he did not wish to get involved in its unraveling." Do you know if that's correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I noted that. Could I have answered that even without you having to ask. The commander, Sladojevic, was --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry. I'm going to run out of time. Can you just try to focus your answers and just be as brief as you can. Sorry to interrupt. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how can I be briefer than to say that it was, if he was a proper commander, according to his conscience, he would have had to remove those people from the SUP leadership. They were not fit to be in the SUP leadership.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, that wasn't the question. The question whether you -- it was whether you can confirm what is written in this paragraph. First: Commander of the Slavonia Corps. Was he informed about this incident, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did confirm that. And I noted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So the answer is yes. Now, did he state that he was not aware of the situation, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then third, did he state that he did not wish to get involved in the unraveling of that situation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That answers the question. Please proceed, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know why he made that decision; why he didn't intervene or have the army intervene to help protect the assistant minister of the interior, Ilija Kojic?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that very well. Said Miroljub would slap colonels. If you need an interpretation, it's a -- striking somebody with your palm on their cheek.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you for that explanation. Let me try to shortcut this. It's plain, then, from this and the events that you described that Ilija Kojic had no command authority over the RSK Army at this point in time; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Not at that time. Actually, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Never. Thank you. It's also plain that he no command authority over - am I correct? - the Secretariat of National Defence, which was a body that Vujovic was the secretary of; correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vujovic, Miroljub.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Kojic had no command authority over the Secretariat of National Defence, of which Vujovic was the secretary; correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how could I have the authority when, in all European states, the ministries are separate? The ministry of -- for police and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. What happens in other states is not the question. Mr. Jordash asked you if it is correct that Kojic had no command authority over the Secretariat of National Defence; is that correct or not? The Secretariat of National Defence of which Vujovic was the secretary; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct. All I said was that these were two independent sectors, and I just wanted to explain, actually, how it is in theory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If Mr. Jordash is interested to see whether this is in line with a theory, he will ask you. He only asked you whether what he said was accurate, yes or no. And the simple answer then is yes, it is accurate. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know what the authority was, or what the job description was, of the Secretariat of National Defence at that time? What did it do.

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Set in the constitution of Republika Srpska and the Law on National Defence, I said he -- these were tasks of recruitment and mobilisation, records, sending conscripts to serve their term of duty, maintaining records, establishing the deployment, setting the staging areas, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And these issues were all in relation to combat operations; is that right? Military operations.

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Kojic's authority was limited to issues relating to police work, crime, and prevention work; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Public security tasks, which is a broader term than police work. I don't need to go into that because I'm being asked to be brief and rationalise the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you to look at the paragraph which begins: "Around 1500 hours, a meeting started in the secretariat building ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we go to the second page of the B/C/S, please, or the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: "Around 1500 hours, a meeting started in the secretariat building, on which occasion the present senior MUP staff were informed ... they are being dismissed because of, as alleged, obstructing work and avoiding co-operation with the Secretariat of National Defence." Is that correct, from your own knowledge?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What work was being obstructed according to the Secretariat of National Defence, or those who represented that body, in that meeting?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The powers were simply not clear, and if there was a conflict of powers, it could not have been resolved at the same level. But the government would need to be informed about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, I think we're misunderstanding each other. I'm asking you what work was being obstructed according to the representatives of the Secretariat of National Defence.

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: None, by the regulations. If somebody made up some on their own, that was a different issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Let me try this differently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, you emphasised in one of your previous questions the personal knowledge of the witness. Could we just establish -- You were not present at that point in time in the -- in the MUP building, were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I read the report, and I know the final outcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So when we talk about your personal knowledge, it is based on the report and what you learned about the outcome?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What was the main complaint of the Secretariat of National Defence? What did they put forward as the reason they wanted to remove Kojic? Whether that reason is correct or not, what was the reason they put forward at the time?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Was it plain, though, to you, when you arrived in the region and began your tasks, that the real reason that Vujovic - accompanied later on by Arkan - had sought to remove Ilija Kojic was because Kojic was trying to prevent their criminal activity?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. After I came, incidents like that didn't happen anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's read on in the document, see if can you assist. Do you know if Arkan, as this paragraph suggests, along with Mrgud, came to the meeting afterwards, or during the meeting, and supported the demands for Kojic and others to be removed from their posts?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know, yes. Also, that he was the one who initiated or actually agreed before arrival that it should be done that way. He's considered to be the most responsible.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What was Arkan's relationship to the Secretariat of National Defence at that time?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: None. He was with Milan Milanovic, Mrgud, and Milanovic was the first step in the order, and then it was him protecting his protege.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: With Mrgud being Arkan's protege, or vice versa?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they helped each other out. It was mutual.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: They were friends, Mrgud and Arkan, and supported each other in their professional activities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And let's read on in the document. The next paragraph begins: "After a five-hour discussion at which, according to our information, the accused party was not given an opportunity to present its facts and arguments, the conclusion was brought that an RSK government session should be convened within three days at which a decision would be taken on the dismissal of the present and the appointment of new senior staff of the Vukovar Secretariat." Do you know if that's correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that there was any government session in Knin to discuss this. I just know that Bogicevic, who was the vice-president of the government, attended the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Reading on: "In the demand that was put forward, it was requested to replace Ilija Kojic, assistant minister of the RSK MUP, the entire leadership of the Vukovar Secretariat, two operatives in charge of vehicle theft, and the desk officer for vehicle registration." Do you know if this is correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct. And I know the reason, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Please explain.

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two operatives, one of them being Mandic and the other one being Novo, they seized vehicles that had been stolen, large-scale. And of course Iso, who was the desk officer for registration of these vehicles, was an obstacle because he would not register vehicles that did not have appropriate paperwork with them. In other words, there should be a sales document, there should be a technical service or technical inspection document, and so on. Registration paper, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's read on. "It was envisaged that Kojic be replaced by Ljubomir Milojevic ..." Do you know if that's correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. And I know Milivojevic. He was the head of section in Osijek before the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know why it was proposed that he should replace Kojic. Why was it that Arkan and Mrgud wanted that man instead of Kojic?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because he and Radulovic, Predrag Radulovic, spent a lot of with them. They spent a lot of time together. You can find information about Predrag Radulovic. There is a report.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's read on: "The DB head, Slobodan Ivkovic, who was accused for allegedly co-operating with the RDB of the MUP of ... Serbia was to be replaced by Predrag Radulovic ..." Do you know whether Arkan, Mrgud, Vujovic, accused - or at least thought - that Ivkovic was, at the time, co-operating with the DB of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ivkovic was trained for state security work, whereas Radulovic was not. For a while, when each village had a sheriff of their own, he was the secretary of the SUP and minister for Baranja alone. There existed a minister for Baranja alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And did Arkan want to replace Ivkovic, as far as you're aware, because he thought Ivkovic was working -- was -- was working for the Serbian DB?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't see anything bad in services exchanging information, nor is Arkan the person who should -- who is actually in a position to assess a thing like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Mr. Djukic, we are in complete agreement, but I'm trying to find out some information because I want to know what you know so you can assist the Court. So we agree on that. But what I want to know is: Do you have any information that corroborates what this document says, which is that Arkan wanted -- or those around Arkan at this time wanted to replace Ivkovic because they thought he was working in some way with the Serbian DB?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any information to that effect. If he did co-operate with them, how I would know?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm not asking you whether he did work for the DB --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please carefully listen to the question. The question is not whether he co-operated but the question is whether, from Arkan's position, they wanted Ivkovic to be replaced because they suspected that he was co-operating with the Serbian DB. Do you know whether this was what moved them; or do you not know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know. That was the -- the thing that motivated them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, there's no suggestion here that -- they thought that Kojic worked for the Serbian DB. Do you know if they suspected him at the time? Was that also a motivation or not?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: When you came into the region, did you have any idea that Kojic had any relationship with the Serbian DB? Were you told that? Or did he tell you that?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't, nor was I told, nor do you ask such things of your colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we go to page 3 of the document and we stick with this paragraph; page 4 of the B/C/S. The writer of the report notes: "It is indicative" -- And I'm reading from halfway down the first page in that English: "It is indicative that they are asking for the dismissal of persons working on vehicle theft or registration duties, especially since a person who has prior convictions for committed crimes and has served terms of imprisonment for the duration of nine years was foreseen for the position of desk officer for vehicle registration."

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I've already said what the reason was and why those operatives who were in charge of vehicle thefts should be removed from the secretariat, and why the desk officer - who refused to register stolen vehicles - should be removed and bring in their place a criminal who would be in charge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. What did Martic do about this? What did he do, if anything, to protect Kojic and his colleagues from Arkan?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's a fact that he protected him because everyone remained in their posts. And a mere month and a half later, there was a high-level meeting which he convened, where it was concluded that Arkan should be banned from entering the region. And I've already testified to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me ask you about the relationship between Martic and Kojic and Kostic later on in 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have on the screen, please, P987.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me try to shortcut things. First of all, am I correct that there came a time when Kojic and Martic fell out?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the reason was for that. They were officials, and it was not my place to inquire into what their relationship was, unless I was asked to provide my professional opinion. As I've already said, there was a difference in the way they functioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Actually, let's go back to the document we looked at again. I want to ask you about a paragraph which might help to you recall certain details. Whilst that's coming up - that's D398 again - the report that is coming back on the screen that we've been talking about was written by a man called Milenko -- perhaps -- yes, it's fine. Written by a man called Milenko Lemic. Did you know that man? Or at least co-authored by Lemic. Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him. And I know him now. He is a retired member of the State Security Service, the service for Vojvodina, which was in Novi Sad.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And did you know him at the time; and, if you did know him at the time, what was he doing in the region? Do you know? At the time of this report.

utterances.speaker: PETAR DJUKIC [Resumed]
